The endless battles also began to take their toll on the population. Those who could afford it ran away to other countries while the poor were left without a place to sleep, the kingdom now reduced to ruins. The conflict continued for three generations unabated, with the Giants sustaining their attacks on northern fortifications and trying to push their way inland towards the Royal Castle. Vendrick, however, never made either decision and continued to reign over Drangleic. Both he and his brother were not convinced by the two possible choices and, anchored to the illusion of the form that life had during the Age of Fire, they looked for a way to maintain it, searching for a way to free humans from the curse of Undeath and breaking the seal of fire that imprisoned them. As he deepened his knowledge of souls and curses, Vendrick effectively reigned over Drangleic, protecting the country from any external threats. title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Battles waged endlessly between Vendrick's forces and the Giants, and much of Drangleic's citizens fled the kingdom to escape the conflict. Ultimately, the Giants were defeated by an unnamed hero. In the aftermath, much of Drangleic had been reduced to rubble, and visitors to the kingdom were rare. Many Giants were killed in the conflict, and their corpses eventually grew into large trees that sprawled across the once prosperous kingdom. The last known Giant to have survived the conflict was terribly wounded and kept prisoner in a cavern beneath the Forest of Fallen Giants. It was later discovered another two Giants survived the war, but remained hidden in a cavern in Black Gulch.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Seeking vengeance for the subjugation of his kingdom, the king of the Giants amassed an army in a vengeful counter-invasion of Drangleic. He also sought to reclaim the invaluable "prize" stolen from him. Unwilling to forgive the actions of Vendrick, the Giants crossed the sea and landed on the northern shores of Drangleic. They set siege to Drangleic Castle and relentlessly attacked various settlements, forts and keeps across the land for several generations.

title: Northern Sea
snippet: During his reign, King Vendrick was advised by Queen Nashandra that across the sea there was the looming thretat of the Giants. Vendrick gathered an army and crossed the ocean, defeated the Giants, pillaged their land and took control of their great power, using it to create the golems and further develop his kingdom. However, the giants, angered by the invasion and barbarism of the king of Drangleic, responded by crossing the sea and directly invading the human kingdom with the desire to take revenge on Vendrick, bringing war that consumed Drangleic for centuries with their directed and burning rage..

title: Nashandra
snippet: When Drangleic was ravaged by the second war with the giants and the spread of the Undead Curse, Vendrick came to realize the true nature and identity of Nashandra, and what she had coveted all along. Knowing that his time was short and that his queen had to be stopped, Vendrick created several impasses that would prevent Nashandra from seizing the throne, and sealed himself away in the Undead Crypt. This left Nashandra the sole ruler of Drangleic, albeit without much left to rule at all, as the kingdom had been all but destroyed.

Overcome by nihilism, Vendrick was consumed by the curse and soon became a hollow, mindlessly roaming the empty crypt forever to protect the ring that would grant access to the Throne of Want. title: Drangleic
snippet: In the mountains east of Drangleic, Aldia also created the Dragon Aerie to raise hundreds of wyverns under the control of his spells. The Dragon Shrine was also built at the center of the wyverns' nest, as a site of worship for the Ancient Dragon. It was a place where members of the Dragon Remnants and those who venerated the dragons in an attempt to transform to obtain their immortality and transcend human existence were welcomed, while also collecting artifacts such as the Petrified Egg to study dragon biology. After the king's brother had developed the nest to raise the creatures, the Dragonriders of Vendrick's royal guard stopped riding the obsolete wyrms and moved on to creatures closer to the ancient dragons.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Initially the king took over the existing structures that had helped contain the curse under previous countries such as the Lost Bastille and the No-man's Wharf, using the golems and creatures already present such as the Flexile Sentries and the Ruin Sentinels as jailers. Undead Citizens of the kingdom who died and returned to life cursed would thus be locked in the squalid fortress and, once the numbers swelled to fill the cells, forced inside rickety ships and sent to certain death in the open sea. But the ongoing conflict and the resulting increase in deaths would only lead to more undead and more hollows. In an attempt to stave off the curse of undeath that was plaguing his kingdom, Vendrick hired some deserted members of the shadow knights from Mirrah, skilled assassins, to put down the hollows, making them work in the No-man's Wharf where they sent the imprisoned undead to die in the sea, but before long they became hollow themselves. title: Giants (Lore)
snippet: dark_souls : Although the history of the giant race is shrouded in mystery, they have been strongly connected to the Gods of Anor Londo since the times of their War against the Archdragons. The giant Hawkeye Gough led the Dragonslayers, a group of giants known also as the Greatarchers who served alongside Lord Gwyn's Silver Knights. These giants wielded immense bows that had to be anchored to the ground to be used, employing arrows that resembled iron spears which were fired with such force as to injure high-flying dragons. Gough himself possessed a greatbow even larger than the archers he led, and was the only one with the strength required to handle it. He distinguished himself on the battlefield as a dragonslayer and received from Lord Gwyn himself a golden medallion and dragon bone pauldrons as ornaments for his armor, crafted with a material similar to those worn by the Silver Knights, symbolizing the highest honors for a warrior. snippet: In the darkest hour of his reign, Vendrick also realized that his Queen, Nashandra, was a creature of the Abyss, and harbored an insatiable desire for strength. She was a fragment of a dark creature taken a human form, obsessed with the King's powerful soul. Impelled by her cravings, Nashandra sought souls, and strove to make the strength of the Giants her own, everything to reach the Throne of Want and the link for the First Flame so it could spread the Dark. Her painting in the castle was in fact able to curse the undead, making them hollow and draining their life, and only the king knew whether the depiction of the Queen was a resentful mockery, or an affectionate exaltation. At this point Vendrick had achieved a profound understanding of the truths of the world. title: Vendrick
snippet:
Vendrick -  Dark Souls II - boss - plot 
 plot : After an untold amount of time in confinement, the King of Drangleic remains a hollowed husk of his former self. The player may choose to spare the king, leaving him to wander eternally, or slay him and end his misery.

Using the Ashen Mist Heart, the Bearer of the Curse may also enter the Memory of the King, where they may interact with King Vendrick as he was before he went hollow. Bitter and grieving his failures, Vendrick tells the Bearer to seek the crowns of old kings of yore. Once they have brought him all the crowns, Vendrick will unlock their power, making the Bearer of the Curse immune to the hollowing effects of the curse. He advises the Bearer of the Curse to seek a third path beyond Light and Dark, echoing his brother.

title: Forest of Fallen Giants
snippet:
Forest of Fallen Giants -  Dark Souls II - location - description 
 description : The Forest of Fallen Giants is a forested area filled with exuberant vegetation bathed by sunlight. The ruins of a long-forsaken fortress, known as the Cardinal Tower, can be found in the area as well. It is said that this structure was built long ago by the Kingdom of Drangleic during the battle against the Giants. Hollow Soldiers still stand guard to this day, and remnants of several Giants lay throughout various locations. It is here that players can take alternate paths to proceed to the next area. Each path offers different advantages. One of them, for example, allows the player to avoid the area boss.

title: Raulmond, Knight of Drangleic
snippet:

He was known for cershing rings that bore the protection of dragons throughout all of his life and service to Drangleic. He might have been an exceptional champion, however, as the first of his rings is the second highest reward of the Company of Champions covenant, a group of brave warriors based in Majula who scoff at danger and seek greater challenges, their names engraved to commemorate their deeds.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet: Regardless, the Dragon Knights, who wore armor forged from the scales of Kalameet and used weapons created from his tail, persisted, and at some point arrived in Drangleic and settled in the Dragon Shrine. The group of knights would also join the covenant of the Dragon Remnants, apostles who venerated the primordial creatures and desired the perpetuity of their existence, seeking their scales to rise above their limited human existence. This group used the Dragon Eyes to invade the space and time of other knights and challenged them to claim their dragon scales, rewarding the best among them with the stones infused with the powers of the dragons to try to achieve transformation, as well as with the ancient Black Dragon Greatsword forged from Kalameet's tail.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Once his army had been prepared and armed with spears and greatbows that used arrows as big as iron spears, Gwyn went to the surface with the intention of waging war against the Dragons and conquering the world with his Lord allies. The war turned out to be very bloody; for each of the majestic creatures slain, three scores of Gwyn's soldiers perished. The bodies of dragons were harder than stone, and resistant to fire and magic, making their killing difficult. At one point Gwyn was even forced to integrate into his ranks the primordial humans, descendants of the Furtive Pygmy who had found the Dark Soul, and who had developed their own weapons and armor infused with the life-giving power of the Abyss.

title: Captain Drummond
snippet:
Speaking with Drummond also has an unseen effect: he claims he'll order his men to stand down and allow the player to pass through, and indeed, the soldiers encountered in the memories from this point forward will not be hostile to the player and will instead assist them in fighting the Giants. snippet: Centuries after Gwyn sacrificed his soul to link the Flame, some remnants of it manifested again in Drangleic, continuing to exert their influence on the region. At some point the Old Iron King came into contact with the soul of Gwyn, which had become "Ichorous Earth" and produced the scorching iron and magma of the Iron Keep. The Old Iron King was thus destroyed by the mass of iron possessed by the soul of Gwyn who then went on to control the remains of the Old Iron King, creating a demonic-looking creature made of melted iron.

title: Ancient Dragon
snippet: Rumors abound in Drangleic about the king's brother, Lord Aldia, who tried to create a dragon. Perhaps the existence of the Ancient Dragon, and its dubious origins, are testament to his success.

snippet:
Eventually, Felkin's research into hexes and the Dark brought him to the fallen kingdom of Drangleic, "where Dark runs deeper than anywhere else", likely due to the Throne of Want holding the power of the fading First Flame and making the kingdom the epicenter of the Undead curse and a potential coming of an Age of Dark.

title: Lion Clan
snippet:
They seemed to have a hierarchy too, placing the clansmen with a golden mane above the rest, maybe even viewing them as leaders. These Golden Lion Warriors would earn a finely-crafted ornamental helm and an impressive red cape to denote their status among the other clansmen.

Eventually, the Lion Clan wound up in Drangleic, settling in the ruins of the misty Shaded Woods. It was probably during this time that they started to dabble with curses, as the ruins within their territory are surrounded by laughing jars containing cursed energy, which their weapons seem permeated with. Some time later they would capture Weaponsmith Ornifex, who resided in the nearby town of Tseldora, and trap her in the caves below their domain.

It wouldn't be long until their entire society would be upturned when a great number of clansmen were turned to stone, likely by the nearby Basilisks. Their mages also seemingly vanished, with nothing but their clothing remaining.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: Many years later during the Age of Fire, shortly after the fall of Izalith to the Flame of Chaos, a group of Dragon Knights serving Gwyn and led by Dragon Knight Gravis arrives in New Londo in an attempt to negociate assistance against Izalith, unaware that the Four Kings have been convinced to rebel against Gwyn. They are attacked by a group of Darkwraiths and Skeletons, who slay all but Gravis and hired mercenary Wurdow; as they prepare for a last stand, the two are rescued by Artorias, who decapitates all foes surrounding them. As Gravis expresses her surprise and gratitude, Artorias points them to the gate they had entered to silently order them to leave, and progresses deeper into New Londo alone.

title: The Pursuer
snippet:
Being cursed whilst fighting the two Pursuers in Drangleic Castle will prompt one of them to leave. This only occurs if both Pursuers are still present. As of patch 1.10, this no longer works.
In Drangleic Castle, dying after defeating one pursuer will cause the player to lose their drop, whether it be the Ring of Blades+2, or the Twinkling Titanite.
When he is fought for the first time in his boss room, he will be met by a cutscene, leading him to instantly being able to attack. But the times after that, he will slowly emerge from the ground, meaning that the player is able to use a ranged attack, so long as they can dodge the lunge attack afterwards.

title: Nashandra
snippet: Left without a king and with no means to claim the Throne of Want, Nashandra’s plans were stalled until the arrival of the Bearer of the Curse, an undead powerful enough to defeat the Four Old Ones and gain access to Drangleic Castle. Nashandra manipulated the Bearer of the Curse into opening the way to the Throne of Want by aiding them in seizing the Throne of Want. She directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Undead Crypt, suggesting that they put an end to the now-hollowed King Vendrick and claim his ring. She then directs the Bearer of the Curse to journey to Aldia's Keep to acquire the Ashen Mist Heart, and warns them that the Ancient Dragon there is no more than a prop and a false deity. At last, she directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Forest of Fallen Giants to visit the memories of the Giants and obtain the last key to the Throne: the Giant's Kinship.

title: Gods
snippet:
At one point a God committed the sin of "greed". For this they were banished and cursed, resulting into their head transforming into an imitation of treasure chests. They became the very first Mimic. The Mimic became "the symbol of shame imposed on a long lost clan, exiled for the sin of avarice", perhaps meaning that this clan were similarly turned into Mimics.

Gwyn led the Gods and their Silver Knights in a war against the Dragons. With their powerful magic and the aid of the Dragon traitor, Seath the Scaleless, the Gods slew most of the Dragons and claimed the world for their own. Gwyn and his family founded the mighty city of Anor Londo, from whence they ruled over the humans, distant descendants of the Furtive Pygmy.

title: Lindelt
snippet: The Drakeblood Knights who founded Lindelt made a conceited effort to bury their past and become upstanding dragon priests, using the Shulva civilization's advanced religious knowledge to spread their religion. The "Archdrake Church" thus became the keepers of Lindelt's history, and swiftly struck down the curious few who delved too deep into the kingdom's origins. They further rewrote history by rebranding themselves as heirs to an order of knights who "once felled a poisonous dragon which menaced an entire nation". The people of Lindelt were kept in the dark on the Archdrake sect's rituals in which artifacts relating to their past were used for ceremonial purposes.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Nashandra began her life as a small fragment of Manus, Father of the Abyss. When Manus was defeated, he was reborn as many fragments varying in sizes. Nashandra was the incarnation of her "father's" want, and thus began desiring what she did not have: power.

Nashandra travelled to the land of Drangleic, and set her sights on its powerful ruler, King Vendrick. Deciding to seduce Vendrick, Nashandra assumed a human form of unparalleled beauty and warned him of a supposed looming threat beyond the sea: the Giants. She convinced him to invade the land of the giants to claim their power, which Vendrick did successfully. Vendrick then made Nashandra his queen, and under their leadership, Drangleic entered into a Dark-like peace. The rulership of Drangleic however, was not enough to quell Nashandra’s want, and she desired an even greater power: the First Flame, which she intended to claim for herself by using Vendrick and the Throne of Want.

title: Dark Souls II
snippet:
Dark Souls II -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - plot 
 plot : The story of *Dark Souls II* is not directly connected to *Dark Souls*, though they are set in the same world.

The game takes place in Drangleic, a once prosperous land under the rule of King Vendrick, which has fallen to ruin throughout the ages with the raging war between humans and giants, the sudden disappearance of the King, and the spreading of the Undead Curse. Like many others, the protagonist has come to the crumbling kingdom in search of a cure for their crippling affliction, the Curse of the Undead.

title: Chancellor Wellager
snippet:
Chancellor Wellager -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Chancellor Wellager was one of Vendrick's most important servants, having been present for all of his greatest accomplishments; the founding of the kingdom of Drangleic, the arrival of his queen Nashandra, the construction of the castle and the invasion of the land of Giants, which resulted in the creation of the Golems. This led to a period of peace that the advisor described to be akin to the Dark, a hint to the queen's true nature.

His king had once ordered him to enlist the great blacksmith Llewellyn from the land of Mirrah with a lifetime contract, so that the kingdom of Drangleic could have access of the rare geisteel from the eastern land, which had been secret until then. Wellager would succeed in this, even being gifted the Espada Ropera by the blacksmith. His exploits would strengthen the kingdom greatly.

Forossa -  Dark Souls III - location - lore 
 lore : Forossa is a land located to the distant east of Drangleic.

The kingdom of Forossa was defined by war, constantly in conflict with its neighbors. Leading up to the fall of the nation, it was engaged in a protracted war with its neighbors. The culture and organization of the Forossan army rightly recognized and rewarded their soldiers for their strength, determination and diligence on the battlefield; those who distinguished themselves could, in the course of their lives, ascend from mere peasants to generals.

title: High Lord Wolnir
snippet: The warriors of Carthus swore their lives to Wolnir, growing ever ruthless and bloody in his name. Under Wolnir's rule, the kingdom of Carthus grew aggressive and expansionist, to the point where it was likened to uncontrollable fire, its beacons being used as war signals. His conquests were spearheaded by his warriors with superior combat skills and combat pyromancies. Wolnir soon subjugated the kingdoms around Carthus, melding the various "crowns" that ruled different lands into a single one, thus ascending to "High Lord". At some point Wolnir stripped three armlets and a holy sword from the corpses of some clerics, demonstrating how religion and gods counted for nothing in his kingdom.

title: Sir Syan
snippet:
Sir Syan -  Dark Souls II - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Sir Syan was widely known as the kingdom's most loyal knight, and was King Vendrick's very own retainer. When the giants invaded Drangleic, he volunteered to lead the advance party against them, but was slaughtered most dishonorably. He would never get to behold the greatshield that the king had commissioned for him, named after his glory and meant to immortalize it.

After Syan's death, Vendrick commisioned replicas of his knight's suit of armor as well as his iconic halberd. This equipment would be given to promising knights among his army, to honor his trusted retainer's memory. However, those who had the honor of donning this armor soon lost their mind, with no explanation.

Perhaps it was the burden of living up to Syan's example, or maybe it was his own spirit haunting the suits of armor. The truth of the matter remains shrouded in mystery.

title: Carthus of the Sands
snippet: At some point, the giant humanoid Wolnir rose to power in Carthus. The warriors of Carthus swore their lives to Wolnir, growing ever ruthless and bloody in his name. His conquests were spearheaded by his warriors with superior combat skills and combat pyromancies. Wolnir soon subjugated the kingdoms around Carthus, melding the various "crowns" that ruled different lands into a single one, thus ascending to "High Lord". Along the way, Wolnir stripped three armlets and a holy sword from the corpses of some clerics, demonstrating how religion and gods counted for nothing in his kingdom.

title: Forossa
snippet:
Forossa -  Dark Souls III - location - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : In the region and times of Lothric, Forossa was recognized as a kingdom that had been destroyed, but legends about its Lion Knights and those among them that became part of history remained alive.

Following the collapse of Forossa, its survivors, along with other groups originating from Drangleic, contributed to founding the kingdom of Lothric. One of the armor sets that were named for the ancient god of war worshipped by the Forossans was preserved; among the royal guard of Lothric is Lion Knight Albert, descendant of the order of Forossa Knights.

The brigands who survived the fall of Forossa, though no longer identified by their homeland, still roam the world wielding their ancient war axes.

title: Olaphis
snippet:
Olaphis -  Dark Souls II - location - lore 
 lore : Olaphis was a kingdom that once stood on the land which corresponds to the domains of Drangleic under the reign of King Vendrick. The country was one of many kingdoms that rose and fell throughout the history of the region. The immense fortress of the Bastille was the residence of the country's ruler and the nucleus of the kingdom, its land extending as far as the regions that would be later known as Brightstone Cove Tseldora and the Shrine of Amana.

Olaphis was a sophisticated society home to advanced technology and magic, developed in both sorceries and pyromancies. Its craftsmen were credited with complex designs, known for their refined halberds and powerful staves. The kingdom seems to have mined the brightstone in their territories and turned them into crystals, which were used in their catalysts to amplify sorceries.

title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet: The old knights of Lothric also turned to the Firstborn of Lord Gwyn for aid, once venerated as a god of war and the sun, who in turn gave them the tools to face the wyverns. From the sun god they would learn how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons developed in the war between the gods and the Everlasting Dragons. They also learned of his miracles on manipulating lightning as a weapon.

title: Syan's Helm
snippet:
Syan's Helm -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Replica of the helmet of the loyal knight Syan. his solidly-crafted helm offers high defense.

Sir Syan was widely known as the kingdom's most loyal knight, and when the Giants invaded, he volunteered to lead the advance party, but was slaughtered most dishonorably.

The King commissioned replicas of Syan's accoutrements and bestowed them to promising knights, but not long after they donned the armor did they go thoroughly mad.

title: Forossa
snippet:
Forossa was also the origin of the special and powerful black firebombs capable of causing large flames and explosions. These bombs, due to the risk they posed to their owners, were subject to strict standards for their safe storage, codified in the kingdom's legislature.

Forossa eventually fell to war, its military and government exhausted to the point of collapse. The fall of the country left its citizens to their own devices, most of whom became bandits and thieves that infested the outskirts of their fallen home, or scattered across the continent. Without an element of cohesion, the remaining Forossan knights became mercenaries, selling their fighting strength to foreign armies. Among these Lion Knight mercenaries was Vengarl of Forossa, once a ferocious warrior on the battlefield, who came to Drangleic and served under the command of King Vendrick.

title: Captain Drummond
snippet:
Captain Drummond -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Captain Drummond descends from a family line of high-ranking army captains of Vendrick, entrusted with his seaside fort. The helm in their possession is proof of the king's great trust.

However, a long time after the king had subdued the Giants and stolen their prized possession in his conquest, the beings would cross the sea to enact their vengance in a war that continued for generations. The fort overseen by Drummond's family was the main stage of the long-winded massacre, with his grandfather and father both having to face the threat of the Giants, until the duty would be passed down to him, as well as their equipment.

title: Bone Scythe
snippet:
Bone Scythe -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : Scythe forged from the soul of the Covetous Demon.

The curved spine of the Covetous Demon is as hard as rock, and rather than slicing through flesh, this weapon seems to grind it apart.

That thing that ended up a monstrous fiend, what was it to begin with, and why did it never leave the queen? Perhaps it was entranced by some perversion of love.

title: Mirrah
snippet: The excellent alloy called "geisteel" had also been invented in the country of Mirrah, and never sold abroad. The rare material allowed the crafting of equipment that offered top-notch protection at a very light weight. As such, its method of manufacture was kept secret from foreign lands, since it provided the kingdom's army with an innovative edge over its enemies. The secrets of geisteel were exported when King Vendrick ordered Chancellor Wellager to hire a craftsman of geisteel. Wellager managed to bring the craftsman Llewellyn back to Drangleic with him. Allocated a blinding salary, Llewellyn became the castle's resident master smith and began working for Vendrick, forging geisteel armor along with long daggers and shields, and distinguished himself for his lack of ostentation and focus on simplicity and strength. His smithy supplied only a select few, including the chancellor himself and the Stone Soldiers and Stone Knights.

title: New Londo Ruins
snippet: The knowledge of the ancient healing sorceries of New Londo somehow survived and reached Drangleic where they were employed this time through miracles like Caressing Prayer, a text developed only around the kingdom of Vendrick and whose authenticity as a sacred text was even questioned, that was able to purify the body and remove all poison of the caster and those close to them.

title: Melfia
snippet: Once an aspiring magician, Felkin the Outcast claims whilst in Drangleic that he studied both sorceries and pyromancy at "a great school in the South"; although he never names the school nor the land, it was likely Melfia, which is south of Drangleic. His wares as a merchant imply that he also studied miracles, as he sells the Magic Barrier miracle as well as items from Lindelt, a land known for its miracles (and where sorcery was anathema), such as the Archdrake Chime used as a catalyst for miracles. Although magically gifted, Felkin did not feel any affinity with either sorcery or pyromancy, but would eventually find his calling in hexes, derived from the very first dark sorceries born during the fall of the long-lost land of Oolacile to Abyss, eventually leading him to come to Drangleic, "where Dark runs deeper than anywhere else", even though, unlike almost everyone else within the fallen kingdom, he is not Undead.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Aldia is the elder brother of King Vendrick, and aided his brother in founding the kingdom of Drangleic. He secluded himself in his manor, searching for secrets of life, viewing the Undead as the key to finding it. For his reverence of the Undead, Aldia was shunned by Vendrick, banished to his Keep forever. People who were invited to his manor commonly disappeared and were replaced with malformed beasts. The Southern and Northern Ritual Bands were created by Aldia and his acolytes after cruel, horrible experiments were performed on these people. Many valuable objects came out of Aldia's Keep, including the Sunset Staff, the Spitfire Spear, Soul Geyser, Unleash Magic, and Forbidden Sun.

Through his experiments, Aldia sought to learn the nature of the undead curse, and to shed the yoke of fate. He failed, however, and turned into a monstrosity, inhabiting the bonfires.

title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet:
Dragonslayer Armour -  Dark Souls III - boss - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that the Dragonslayer Armor is the armor of one of Lothric's early kings from the kingdom's dragonslaying past. This is because his immense armor was preserved for centuries despite its model no longer being in use and placed in the center of a small bridge as a monument. Furthermore, the armor is located between the army barracks with the temple of Lord Gwyn's Firstborn and the last section of Lothric Castle where the royals resided, implying cultural value for the history of knights and worship in the heir of the Sun but also for the royals of the kingdom, acting as a literal and metaphorical bridge between the two.

title: Llewellyn
snippet:
Llewellyn -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : In the age of the kingdom of Lothric, Llewellyn's legacy seems to have lived on, as his name, occupation and geisteel work survive in the Llewellyn Shield, currently found in the possession of Horace the Hushed. More of his equipment found its way into this new age, though it became associated with the Drang Knights instead, mercenaries who descended from the inhabitants of the vanished kingdom of Drangleic. Since their armors were given only to selected members of the castle, it's likely that they are descended from Vendrick's court.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - giant_memories 
 giant_memories : Using the Ashen Mist Heart on the corpse of the giant Jeigh will allow the Bearer of the Curse to enter the giant's memories and fight the Giant Lord during the final days of the war between Drangleic and the Giants. Upon defeating the Giant Lord, they will acquire the Giant's Kinship which will allow them to claim the Throne of Want.

title: Old Iron King
snippet: The Iron King was later approached by Sir Alonne, a great warrior from the east, who trained the King's soldiers and helped him forge a kingdom for himself from the old Kingdom of Venn. Doing so cost the Iron King what little resources he had, but in the process, he discovered an iron-producing miracle, which allowed him to freely shape and harness the powers of iron. With this new power, the Old Iron King became extremely wealthy and powerful, forging from iron both his entire castle, and various golems such as the Ironclads and the Smelter Demons. The King also entertained various craftsmen and savants from many lands, most of whom were charlatans, but many still brought innovations for his kingdom, such as the artisan who crafted the weapon of his Alonne Knigths and Magus Eygil, a pyromancer who wanted to breath life into fire. At the height of his power, the Iron King was known for his arrogance and indulgency in hedonism, mining so intensely parts of his kingdom that poison

snippet:
Soon after, the deities began leaving Lordran. Gwyndolin was the only one of Gwyn's children to stay behind...

Seath, who became obsessed with his research and experiments, amassed countless tomes and was eventually driven mad - at least, how normal people see it - by his research, becoming the founder of sorcery.

At least a thousand years pass and the events of "Dark Souls" begin to unfold...

title: Mirrah
snippet: Beneath the old capital of Mirrah was a holy spring which produced water with healing properties. This miraculous water was extracted, bottled and distributed, becoming a life-saving resource for both the population and the army of Mirrah. However, Mirrah's involvement in war has made the acquisition of its water more difficult, likely due to priority allocation of the water to the kingdom's own residents and army.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - drangleic_castle 
 drangleic_castle : Now with the strength of the four Great Ones, the Bearer of the Curse may pass through the Shrine of Winter to reach Drangleic Castle, the stronghold of Vendrick himself. The Emerald Herald awaits outside, directing the Bearer of the Curse to enter the castle. There is no trace of the King inside the castle however, instead the Bearer of the Curse finds his Queen, Nashandra. Nashandra tells the Bearer of the Curse that Vendrick was less of a king than one might imagine, and that he never took the true throne. She will direct the Bearer of the Curse to the Undead Crypt, to put an end to Vendrick.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: It is possible to theorize that Faraam is the name that the people of Forossa used in veneration of Gwyn's firstborn after his name was lost over the centuries. Not only does Faraam share with the Nameless King the title of "god of war", but the god was also able to bless the armor of Forossa Knights, whose helmet depicted a knight fighting an enormous dragon, implying that Faraam was not a "false" deity created by the legends of men but an active entity in the kingdom who was capable of performing the miracles of the ancient gods. The Lion Knights of Forossa, besides bearing the title "Lion" same as Gwyn's firstborn and first knight, were not only mighty but rabid warriors obsessed with fighting; Forossan knights knew only war and no other ways of living, to the point that they didn't even know what they were fighting for, similarly to the Nameless King who "had respect only for arms, and nothing else".

title: War God Faraam
snippet:
War God Faraam -  Dark Souls III - character - theories 
 theories : It's possible that Faraam is connected to Gwyn's Firstborn Son, maybe even being the name he was known by in Drangleic and its neighboring lands. Both share the title of "God of War" after all, and there is quite a bit of overlap between the people of Forossa, who were characterized by the constant conflicts they lived through and hardly knew any other way of life, and the mindset of the Firstborn, said to have respect for arms alone.

If Faraam truly is the name given to him by Forossa, then the helm named after him that depicts a warrior fighting a dragon might be meant to depict the god, as the Sun's heir was once a great hunter of dragons himself. Furthermore, the order of Lion Knights, worshippers of the war god, would also be sharing the "lion" title of the Old God of War's first knight: Dragon Slayer Ornstein.

title: Black Set (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Black Set (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Straid was a sworn brother-in-arms of the ancient king of old Olaphis. Together, they slew the Ancient Dragon, and tasted of omniscience.
However, even the renowned wisdom of Olaphis was not enough to control the peculiar magic birthed by his arts.

Straid was invited to the old kingdom of Olaphis for his wisdom, but its depth was such that people soon feared him, and in the end Straid was led into a dreadful trap.

Straid spent several lifetimes as stone. During this hiatus, kingdoms rose and fell, until the land called Drangleic came to be.

title: Lothric
snippet: The new inhabitants of the region soon found themselves facing large numbers of wyverns and had to rise to the challenge, ascending common knighthood. The old knights of Lothric turned to the Firstborn of Lord Gwyn for aid, once venerated as a god of war and the sun, and built an altar for him in their city, beginning to worship the ancient deity who in return gave them the tools to face the wyverns. From the sun god they would learn how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons developed in the war between the gods and the Everlasting Dragons. They also learned of his miracles on manipulating lightning as a weapon.

title: Gravelord Nito
snippet: After the war, while Gwyn developed his civilization of Anor Londo and Izalith that of her namesake city, Nito returned to the depths of the Catacombs, an immense necropolis, to slumber within the Tomb of the Giants, an even deeper place that housed the skeletons of enormous and bestial creatures, and turned the caverns into his domain of light-devouring death. In addition, the deceased members of the race of the Gods of Anor Londo and their priests also rested in the Tombs of the Giants, implying how Nito continued to collaborate with Gwyn by offering the Lord his domain to bury his people and servants. Nito would thus take on the role of administering the death of all manner of beings, giving up much of his Lord Soul into propagating death, earning him the title "Gravelord".

title: Lothric
snippet:
Lothric -  Dark Souls III - location - royal_madness 
 royal_madness : Oceiros, upon being crowned King of Lothric, became the representative of the Firelinking culture of the kingdom, which entailed making amends for the failure of Champion Gundyr. The king married Gwynevere, Queen of Lothric, with whom he conceived the divine princes of the kingdom. Lorian, the crown prince, received the ancient brass armor handed down by the royal family, complete with a crown patterned with flame, a symbol of the kingdom's tradition of Firelinking. Lorian was raised as a knight and proved his incredible prowess on the battlefield, leading a war against the remnants of the Chaos Demons, even capturing some of them to serve as slaves for Lothric. Lorian went on to face the Demon Prince, defeating him single-handedly in a battle that eternally scorched his greatsword with the flame of chaos and stained his armor black.

title: Memory of the King
snippet:
Memory of the King -  Dark Souls II - location - notes 
 notes : Each crown obtained unlocks Vendrick's next dialogue.
In order to receive Vendrick's Blessing, the player must actually have to bring all four crowns to him (just having them stored in the item box won't be enough).
Upon attacking Vendrick, he will say *"Foolish..."* in a disgruntled tone and the ashen mist will fade, removing the player from the memory. The player may still re-enter the memory without any consequence.
Once Vendrick has given his blessing to the crowns, the Memory of the King cannot be entered again.
If the player attempts to run back through Velstadt's arena while in the memory, the ashen mist will fade and the player will be returned to the Undead Crypt.

title: Lothric
snippet:
Lothric -  Dark Souls III - location - dragonslaying_foundation 
 dragonslaying_foundation : The origins of the kingdom of Lothric can be traced to the legacy of Drangleic. Survivors of Forossa and Vendrick's Kingdom, together with followers of the Way of Blue and the Heirs of the Sun, were the first inhabitants of Lothric, bringing with them artifacts such as the Spirit Tree and Golden Wing Crest Shields, the Sunlight Straight Sword and even the same Priest's Chimes to their new home.

title: Olaphis
snippet: The kingdom of Olaphis soon fell to the curse, most of its population turned undead or hollow and others perished in the mad purges of the king. Traces of Olaphis culture remained in the region through history. The "Lost" Bastille became the stronghold of the kingdom of Venn, where the Belfry Luna of the princess was built and defended by Belfry Gargoyles, while the Kingdom of Alken was able to recover the Flame Swathe pyromancy of Straid. Some of the wise men who survived the purges of the king and the desperate sea voyage, reaching the south, imparted their knowledge of sorcery and pyromancy to the land where they ended up. Olenford in particular became revered as the father of sorcery in the country that they would help found and that would become known by the name of Melfia. Much later King Vendrick and his brother Aldia conducted research on Olaphis, managing to rediscover Straid's sorceries like Soul Bolt.

title: Mad Knight of Alken
snippet:
Mad Knight of Alken -  Dark Souls II - character - lore

He wielded a peculiar weapon, which is what the Rings of Blades are modeled after. In the era of Drangleic they are associated with the Pursuer, a mysterious accursed knight who holds onto them.

title: War God Faraam
snippet:
War God Faraam -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Faraam is the god of war and main deity of the ruined kingdom of Forossa. The country was in a constant state of conflict with its neighbors, and because of that, war shaped much of their culture and religon, leading to their relentless warrior mentality. And so, Faraam became a key figure of their society.

The God of War's priests lead the warriors of Forossa into battle. These sages could only gain this status after completing a rigorous journey of hardship to the north, earning the title of Northwarders and the reverence of their people as agents of Faraam.

The most important order among the Forossan warriors was that of the Lion Knights, known for wearing a heavy suit of armor named after Faraam himself. Their helms depicted a glorious scene of a knight facing off against a dragon, perhaps one of the War God's legendary deeds, or the deeds of a great Forossan hero.

title: Shrine of Amana
snippet:
Shrine of Amana -  Dark Souls II - location - lore 
 lore : The shrine was once dedicated to sustaining the Demon of Song, long before the undead curse ravaged the kingdom of Drangleic.

title: Knight King Rendal
snippet:
Knight King Rendal -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : His protective ring persisted to the age of the kingdom of Lothric, which seemed to have a better recollection of the Knight King despite his name still being long-forgotten. In fact, legends of this time claim that he was lined with steel on the inside, such that even the talons of mighty dragons did him little harm.

title: Smelter Demon
snippet: The Smelter Demon found in the Iron Keep was responsible for the death of the Old Iron King, and by extension the full fall of his kingdom. Although his existence as the man he was before ended, the King became a golem-like being himself, possessed by an incredibly powerful soul that lurked below the magma.

title: Captain Drummond
snippet:
Captain Drummond -  Dark Souls II - character - plot 
 plot : Drummond is one of the last NPCs that the player can meet on their journey, only accessible after retrieving the Ashen Mist Heart from the Dragon Shrine. With it, one can return to the Forest of Fallen Giants and interact with the Tree of Giants near where Mild-Mannered Pate was first encountered.

Once there, it takes very little for the player to see him. Talking to him provides insight on the war against the Giants, as well as mentioning their powerful leader. After exhausting his dialogue, players can learn the "**Hurrah!**" gesture from him, and he will also become available for summoning against the Giant Lord in the Memory of Jeigh. His summon sign is located at the side of the staircase that leads to the fog gate.

title: Llewellyn
snippet:
Llewellyn -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Llewellyn was a skilled blacksmith that hailed from the land of Mirrah, known for his pragmatic philosophy of simplicity over ostentation, leading to modest-looking yet extremely strong equipment. He was contracted by Chancellor Wellager by the orders of King Vendrick, who wished to introduce the rare geisteel alloy to the armies of Drangleic. The master smith was so pleasd by his offer that he gifted the chancellor with one of his works, the Espada Ropera, when he moved from his homeland to that of his contractors.

Geisteel would soon find itself on some of the weapons of Drangleic's most renowned knights, though they were seldom used in combat due to the rarity of the alloy, even with Llewellyn living in the castle. Special armors were also crafted by the master smith, given only to a select few members of Drangleic's court, which included Wellager himself.

title: Ocelotte
snippet: Once his desire for transcendence was satiated, Oceiros once again fathered a child with Gwynevere, believing that a descendant of dragons would make a worthy Champion. Either because of the child was born deformed and monstrous, or because she suffered violence from Oceiros or was horrified by the King's decaying sanity, but the birth of Ocelotte was too much for the Queen Gwynevere to bare: she decided to abandon the kingdom never to return again, leaving the newborn with the twisted father. title: Giant Lord
snippet:
Melee fighters may find it easier to do this fight unlocked, as the camera tends to spin in strange directions owing to the small area in which the Giant Lord is fought. This can also make it easier to see his tells before his attacks.

If one stands on the ledge to the left, the Giant Lord will limit his attacks to just swinging his sword, making them easier to avoid overall, regardless of the character's class.

title: Giant Lord
snippet:
As you're approaching, he will often do an overhead swing followed with a shockwave which travels in a straight line, however it's easily dodged or hidden away from.

Pyromancers can have an easier time if they have access to Fire Tempest or Chaos storm as the boss rarely moves and will be hit with all the pillars of fire. For the same reason, Poison Mist and Toxic Mist work as well, as the boss rarely moves, it's extraordinarily easy to inflict both Poison and Toxic, dealing at least 45 damage a second until it wears off.

If the player has any magic at their disposal they can remain safe on the platform to the left of the Giant Lord as the boss seems incapable of climbing stairs and so will be easy to hit. The only two attacks player needs to worry about are an overhead slam and sweeping swing. Both can kill the player instantly if the player is on low health. Otherwise, any form of magic makes this a fairly easy fight, and a good farming location for Giant Lord souls.

 strategy : Caution must be taken because the way to the Giant Lord is just as dangerous as the boss itself and at times more lethal. The platform is bombarded by fireballs at the entrance (near the fog gate) and at the end (near the Giant Lord).

Along the way the head of a statue will come down and roll across the platform killing everything in its path. There are several safe spots to the left and right so it's advisable to either wait for the head to stop rolling or quickly run to the safe spot in the middle.

The strategy for the Giant Lord is very similar to the Last Giant, staying between his legs will usually be enough to avoid most of his attacks.

title: Giant Lord
snippet:
The strategy for the Giant Lord is very similar to the Last Giant, staying between his legs will usually be enough to avoid most of his attacks.

He does, however, have some nasty tricks: he has a sword slash that covers the right side of his body and his back. This is by far his deadliest attack, not to mention the back is usually the safest spot for a large boss, so it can catch someone by surprise. Standing behind him is usually what triggers this attack, so attack and quickly roll between his legs.

As you're approaching, he will often do an overhead swing followed with a shockwave which travels in a straight line, however it's easily dodged or hidden away from.

title: Giants (Lore)
snippet: After Lord Gwyn's sacrifice to revive the fading First Flame, Giants were used as slaves in Sen's Fortress, which was built on the only route leading to the city of the gods and served as a testing ground for the Undead that managed to overcome the first challenge of the Bells of Awakening and sought to enter Anor Londo to receive the Lordvessel. After ringing both Bells of Awakening, an enslaved giant would recognize that an Undead has completed the first trial of their quest and open the gate to grant entrance into the fortress. Other chained giants powered many of the deadly traps within: one giant manually loaded a mechanism that sent lethal boulders along various routes in the fortress, and another one launched enormous firebombs towards wanderers who reached the peak.

snippet:
Giants (Lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : By the era of Lothric, when the gods of Anor Londo were but a distant memory, the giants in their employ had been scattered. The Cathedral of the Deep enslaved most of the known surviving giants, forcing them to protect their interests in the Cathedral, Irithyll Dungeon, and occupied Anor Londo. The Giant Sentinels in the city of gods were likely reduced to the disgraced, unclad beasts found sleeping on the way to the old Cathedral of Anor Londo, a line of defense against those intruding on Aldrich. The Greatarchers of Hawkeye Gough went nearly extinct, save one atop a tower in the Undead Settlement who guarded the White Birches found around the foot of the High Wall. Gough himself is remembered for having struck down a calamitous dragon with his Greatbow during the events of *Dark Souls*.
